LEGO Overwatch D.Va and Reinhardt 75973 Mech Building Kit with Popular Overwatch Character Minifigures and Buildable Rocket Hammer (455 Pieces) Neither my daughter nor I play Overwatch, but we do enjoy our Lego products together. I got this expecting to get some cool robots that would likely be invited over to tea with Barbie, but what I did not expect was how great these would look assembled. These robots have intricate touches on their armor that look really unique, and often hide the tell-tale Lego look that many of their creations have. The result is that these look more like real toys than something we put together.

There are a few minor quibbles. This comes with a lot of rare or unique pieces, but unlike a lot of kits, I have difficulty imagining using many of them beyond the specific applications of putting these kits together. A lot of very intricate and small pieces make these work. In addition, one of the figures slots into their robot perfectly, while the other is just tossed into a slot to rattle around, which feels pretty unfinished. A decidedly non-professional touch to a kit that would otherwise be worthy of display.

Overall though, a great character kit from Lego.

Kid Galaxy Amphibious RC Truck Morphibians Gator. Remote Control ATV, 27 MHz I have now purchased 3 of these. I bought them for 2 nieces and 1 nephew. The 3 year old has a little trouble with the controls, but the 4 year old is handling the controls well. A little different controls from normal RC; the controls are track (left-side, right-side) controls ... so both forward if forward, both back is back, left forward right center is right turn, left forward right back is fast right turn, opposite for left turns ...

The batteries were a surprise: the controller uses aaa, the vehicle uses aa ... so make sure you get both sizes.

The great part is that these are fun for even adults, when the kids put these down, the adults still wanted to play.

Tough ... YES... these are inexpensive, so I didn't stop the 4 year old when she kicked this over obstacles it could not climb. Even after abuse, no damage.

Wheels have little tred on tires, is not an off road vehicle, concrete, tile, burber, that's about it. Water not yet tried.

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill Little Tykes = Shoddy

1) you cannot push the red 'igniter' button without pushing over the whole grill, it's so stiff. My toddle certainly can't do it at all.

2) the pieces don't fit together properly, as usual with Little Tykes toys. Ugh. The side panels (the sink and burner pieces) don't mate properly, so the result is very slanted and everything slowly slides off.

3) incredibly light weight. Topples very easily.

4) the doors won't open or shut completely without an adult assisting. My two year old is very particular, and get frustrated that he can't close the doors all the way.

5) the two grilling areas are very small. The slippery food provided falls off incredibly easily. That is not conducive to toddlers enjoying themselves. I would rather have a large flat grilling area that kiddies could enjoy instead of two poorly placed small ones.

6) the faucet handle doesn't move. It really looks like it could. How much more difficult could it be to make that happen? Apparently- for a company that gets everything else wrong- it's far tough.

TL,DR: if you like spending money on cheap products, get it.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended I'm not quite the telescope connoisseur, though I'm quite well versed in optics (avid photographer), and I've discovered there's a bit of a gulf between the "wouldn't it be nice to have a telescope" and those sold to diehard astronomers. This one falls into the former category, and as such I"m not really comparing this to higher end models.

In the lower end realm, I still expect clear optics, no noticeable optical defects, and a stable base. This one checks those boxes. The optics look clean and clear to the naked eye, though lab testing would show where higher end models excel, and it's not the brightest lens (all lenses lose some light due to transmission loss in lens materials and dispersal), but it met my expectations. The tripod is well built enough for this model telescope, but it's no remarkable. As it's geared towards budding astronomers, especially youngsters, the included guide and list of projects to get you going is definitely a strength.

4 stars due to no faults of it's own, though it's not that remarkable either. Recommended, though may want to consider other models.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

text_fidelity_a: Treasure X Quest For Dragons Gold Treasure Set This is a super cool kit. As far as kits go, this is one of the less messy ones we've tried. It does have potential to be messy in certain hands, though. I also like that the treasures are all retrieved pretty quickly. We've tried some kits that took hours and that's with my help. Some of those created a giant mess and I regretted them greatly. This one was fun to do, even for me. (Note here that we have the "New Season". It looks like the "Old Season" set is just the kind that I've regretted in the past.) It comes with 3 different items, so each of my 3 guys got to pick one to try out. 2 of them are within hard plastic containers. These both have a blue pebble like filling. Once the covering is broke through(which isn't hard to do), the person can dig through the blue stuff to get the treasure. Even after the treasure is retrieved, these can be played with again. The other one is an alien and you can cut its stomach open and dig through the slime to pull out the surprise from inside it. While you can still play with it afterwards, once you cut its stomach open, it's not getting sealed back up(until you've got a trick to seal it back up). The only complaint we've got about it is the strong chemical smell. Even my children commented on how strong it was. It's a nice set, though, and we've greatly enjoyed it.

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

After years of mostly disappointing results with another popular bulk bag, I decided to try Wiz Dice. My very first bag I ordered had 16 full sets! I am the type of person who likes to have matching sets for completion sake, especially as I often give these sets away to new players. That was where my disappointment in the other brand stems from.
Of course, I ordered more as my needs demanded, and have always gotten at least 10+ sets with a few incomplete ones that I would set aside. I did this because Wiz dice uses a very limited color pallet, and I knew I would be able to complete those sets as the dice rolled in. Great colors, but limited. This limitation was the only thing I missed about brand X, as they had some amazing color designs. Then series 2 was released.

The color names are ridiculous and fun. If Wiz Dice can keep this up into a third expansion I will be a happy customer. text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

text_fidelity_a:
Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 + I had a light bright as a kid, it wasn't a favorite toy of mine but it was pretty invigorating - I might've used it only a couple of times. That thing seemed like a tank. I guess it had to be to protect the bulb. You could even buy a replacement bulb if it broke.

This one sadly feels a bit cold and inexpensively made. No glowing filament bulb to keep things warm. Nice, new energy efficient electronics that are powered by 3 AAA batteries - hopefully you have some rechargeable ones to use.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.

Fisher-Price Octonauts Sea-Slimed Octopod Playset My boys are currently loving all things Octonauts. Before Christmas arrived, my 3 year old was pretending that Legos were each of the Octonauts. While there's nothing wrong with using his imagination, it was becoming very difficult for us to keep up with exactly which Lego was which Octonaut. He was frustrated at our lack of help when it came to locating a specific piece.

This Octopod has been well loved! As far as characters go, this set only comes with Captain Barnacles. We bought other characters separately to make playing with it more fun, though. It also comes with a container of "sea slime". I dislike this stuff greatly, but my children enjoyed it while it lasted. It didn't make a huge mess, and it's not overly sticky, but touching a piece here and there that escaped from the rest was gross. (Reaching under a bed and feeling cold slime isn't the greatest feeling.) The set even comes with a catapult to throw the sea slime, but I really don't recommend doing that.

Assembly is pretty easy. Several pieces have to snap together, and there's several stickers to put into place, but it happens quickly. Be careful with the stickers. Once you stick them, they're stuck. I have a couple of them the slightest bit crooked, but I couldn't fix it. It uses batteries, but those are already included. There's a button to press to hear sound effects(from the show). I didn't find this horribly annoying, but I do actually like the show.

My only complaint is that the top of the Octopod is hard to close properly. My youngest was very frustrated with it at first, and asked for help with it. It seems he's accepted that it won't close just right at this point, and mostly plays with it with the top open.

Overall, my boys have had great fun playing with it. It's been a great addition to the Gups they also got for Christmas.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.

When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.
text_fidelity_b: Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model
